Hi Marissa — great to chat. A few clarifications: 

- Acme requires a current SOC 2 Type II report (or a plan/schedule for when it will be available). Please let us know whether you have a completed Type II report and the date.
- GDPR scope: we’re evaluating EU-hosted data and need to understand whether Redwood acts as a processor for us and whether data can be isolated in EU regions. HIPAA: we need a high level on your environment’s suitability/certifications for PHI (BAA requirement).
- Subprocessors: please provide a CSV that lists provider name, purpose (compute, logs, monitoring, analytics, payments), and whether they handle customer data or only telemetry.

Security will own the questionnaire (security@acmecorp.com). We can start with the vendor questionnaire — I’m attaching our standard vendor_security_questions.pdf. Once we have your subprocessor list and SOC 2, we’ll determine if we need a DPA or additional controls.

Thanks,
Alice Jones
Senior Security Program Manager, AcmeCorp

Attachment: vendor_security_questions.pdf (sent to security@acmecorp.com)

Subject: Re: Post-call: Subprocessors, SOC 2 & next steps

Hi Alice / security team — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. See items below and attached files: 

1) SOC 2 status:
- We completed a SOC 2 Type II audit in Nov 2025. Attaching the SOC 2 Type II report summary; full report available under NDA.

2) Subprocessor CSV (attached): highlights below (summary only):
- AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1) — primary compute & storage (customer model serving, S3 object storage). Handles customer data when customers use our hosted API.
- GCP (eu-west-1) — optional compute for EU region customers (data residency option).
- Cloudflare — CDN & edge routing (only request metadata, not stored model inputs).
- Datadog — monitoring and metrics (aggregated telemetry; no raw customer request body storage).
- Sentry — error reporting (scrubbed traces; we mask PII in client SDKs).
- Stripe — billing payments (payment data handled per PCI scope; customer billing contacts only).
- HashiCorp Vault / AWS KMS — key management (customer-managed keys available for Private deployments).
- Snowflake (for analytics in some customers) — only aggregated, anonymized usage data; not raw request payloads.

Attached CSV includes purpose, region impact, and a column indicating whether the processor can see customer inputs. If you want a BAA/HIPAA suitability matrix, we can follow up with our security team.

3) Vendor questionnaire: I’ve pre-filled the Redwood-specific items and attached our responses as an Excel. Please review and let me know any gaps you want us to expand on.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm whether you need the full SOC 2 report (we can share under NDA) or the summary is sufficient for initial risk review.
- If Acme needs data residency controls, we can map which workloads can be pinned to EU-only compute (GCP eu-west-1).
- If HIPAA/BAA is required, we’ll loop in our security & legal teams to confirm requirements; we have customers running HIPAA workloads via our Private deployment offering.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20260304.csv; SOC2-TypeII-Report-20251112.pdf (summary); security-questionnaire-responses.xlsx

Best,
Marissa
